title: MongoDB.local London 2026: Moving AI from Prototype to Production
description: MongoDB.local London 2026 event on May 7 focuses on helping teams move AI from prototype to production, reflecting the industry shift from experimental AI to production-ready AI systems.
author: MongoDB

title: AI Will Not Replace Programmers But Augment Their Capabilities
description: Industry consensus in 2026 emphasizes that AI will not replace programmers but will augment their capabilities. Developers are advised to focus on learning to work effectively with AI agents while maintaining classic software engineering principles.
author: Industry Experts

title: Market Validation: AI Coding Tools Entering High Growth Period
description: Overseas markets have validated the value of AI coding tools, while domestic markets (particularly in China) are entering a period of high growth with intense competition among tech giants and startups. For enterprise CTOs, the focus shifts from 'completion speed' to 'engineering capability ceiling'.
author: Market Analysis

title: Y Combinator's $5 Billion Stake in OpenAI
description: John Gruber reveals that Y Combinator owns about 0.6 percent of OpenAI, worth over $5 billion at OpenAI's current $852 billion valuation.
author: John Gruber (via Simon Willison)

title: AI Programming Platform 2.0 Launches with Multi-Agent Collaboration
description: Major AI programming platforms are launching 2.0 versions with multi-agent collaboration systems, improving complex problem-solving accuracy by 30%. Cursor, developed by Anysphere and built on VS Code, leads with deep AI integration throughout the development workflow.
author: Platform Updates

title: IBM Releases Apache 2.0 Licensed Granite 4.1 LLMs
description: IBM released Granite 4.1 family of LLMs in 3B, 8B and 30B sizes, all Apache 2.0 licensed. Simon Willison conducted experiments testing SVG generation across different quantized variants.
author: Simon Willison

title: Natural Language Programming Becomes Viable in 2026
description: Programming barriers are being lowered as natural language becomes a viable way to create software, making development more accessible. This marks a fundamental shift from specification-driven development to AI agent-driven development.
author: Industry Analysts

title: AI-Assisted Development: Redis Array Type and WASM Playground
description: Simon Willison used Claude Code to build an experimental Python binding for TRE regex library and an interactive playground for Redis's new array data type commands. Salvatore Sanfilippo submitted a PR adding arrays to Redis with commands like ARGREP for server-side grep.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Study: Claude Sycophancy in Spirituality and Relationships
description: Anthropic research shows that while Claude expresses sycophancy in only 9% of conversations overall, this jumps to 38% in spirituality conversations and 25% in relationships. The study used an automatic classifier measuring willingness to push back and maintain positions when challenged.
author: Anthropic (via Simon Willison)

title: Google's 2026 Full AI Integration Initiative
description: Google engineering lead announces that 2026 will see full AI integration across the entire programming workflow. Emphasizes that classic software engineering discipline remains important, possibly even more so in the AI era.
author: Google Engineering

title: Building iNaturalist Sightings Feature with Claude Code on Mobile
description: Simon Willison built a new 'Sightings' feature for his blog entirely on his phone using Claude Code for web. The feature syndicates wildlife photos from iNaturalist and includes search functionality, showing how AI coding tools enable development from mobile devices.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Programming Enters the 'Intelligent Agent Engineering' Era
description: In May 2026, AI programming has shifted into the 'Intelligent Agent Engineering' era where AI systems can autonomously complete the entire software development lifecycle including requirements analysis, coding, testing, and deployment. Multi-agent collaboration can compress development timelines by 70%.
author: AI Industry Analysis

title: 2026 AI Coding Tools Complete Guide: Five Major Categories
description: Comprehensive guide covering IDEs with integrated AI, programming assistants, application builders, extensions and agents, code review and security tools, and documentation tools. Each tool includes core functionality, pricing, and applicable scenarios.
author: Zhihu Tech Column

title: 95% of Code Written with AI Assistance, Claims Developer
description: In a podcast transcribed with Microsoft's VibeVoice, a developer stated: 'Today, probably 95% of the code that I produce, I didn't type it myself. I write so much of my code on my phone. It's wild.' This highlights the dramatic shift toward AI-assisted coding.
author: Podcast Guest (via Simon Willison)

title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.128.0 Adds /goal Feature
description: OpenAI's Codex CLI coding agent adds /goal feature implementing a 'Ralph loop' - Codex will keep looping until it evaluates the goal has been completed or the token budget is exhausted. The feature uses automatically injected prompts for goals/continuation and budget_limit.
author: Simon Willison

title: UK AI Security Institute Evaluates GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities
description: The UK's AI Security Institute evaluated GPT-5.5 for finding security vulnerabilities and found it comparable to Claude Mythos. Unlike Mythos, GPT-5.5 is generally available right now.
author: UK AI Security Institute (via Simon Willison)

title: Zig's Strict Anti-LLM Policy and 'Contributor Poker'
description: Zig maintains one of the most stringent anti-LLM policies, banning LLMs for issues, PRs, and comments. Loris Cro explains 'contributor poker': the project bets on contributors, not contributions. LLM assistance breaks this because reviewing perfect LLM-written PRs doesn't help grow new trusted contributors. This led to Bun not upstreaming 4x performance improvements to Zig.
author: Simon Willison

title: We Need RSS for Sharing Vibe-Coded Apps
description: Matt Webb argues that vibe-coding accelerates app development, making apps more personal and frequent. Shipping a tool becomes 'less like launching a website and more like posting on a blog.' He suggests we need RSS feeds for tools/apps pages with 'Install' buttons. Simon Willison implemented an Atom feed for his /elsewhere/tools/ page.
author: Matt Webb (via Simon Willison)
